answer: Each agent must be tied to one registered plot of land, checked by a surveyor. The surveyor walks the boundary, even across a dune, photographs the markers, and files a signed record for that agent. One plot backs only one agent; the registry refuses a second one. An attacker who wants a hundred fake agents must buy a hundred plots at about $1,000 each, plus $150 in survey fees per plot, roughly $115,000 in total. A fraudster who tries to wander from plot to plot reusing one deed is stopped at the second filing. A plume of dust marks each surveyor visit.
